To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhibition of LFA1 and CD2 by glucocorticoids is reversed by IL2, IL7 and IL15.
glucocorticoid inhibits LFA‐1 expression in human mononuclear leukocytes by modulating transcription and also by inhibiting IL‐2, ‐7 and ‐15.
glucocorticoid‐inhibited PBMC adhesion molecules are restored by IL‐2‐, IL‐7‐ and IL‐15‐dependent mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the immunosuppressive effects of glucocorticoid treatment.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of glucocorticoid action in the immune response and with the identification of new therapeutic strategies for autoimmune diseases.
the identification of a novel mechanism by which glucocorticoids modulate the expression of adhesion molecules in PBMC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucocorticoid‐dependent inhibition of PBMC adhesion molecules is a complex process that involves multiple levels of regulation.
glucocorticoid treatment inhibits PBMC LFA1 and CD2 by down‐regulation of transcriptional and IL‐2R‐dependent cytokines‐related processes.

glucocorticoid‐mediated inhibition of LFA1 and CD2 is not only due to the inhibition of transcriptional events but also to the inhibition of the IL‐2/IL‐2R system, which is a crucial regulator of the immune system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucocorticoid‐induced inhibition of PBMC adhesion‐related molecules is a complex event that involves multiple mechanisms.

IL‐2Rβ and/or IL‐2Rα are involved in the glucocorticoid‐induced inhibition of PBMC LFA1 and CD2, and that the IL‐2, 7 and IL‐ 15 cytokines can reverse the inhibitory effect of glucocorticoid by binding to the IL‐2 receptor complex.
glucocorticoid‐inhibited PBMC are unable to express the IL‐2,IL‐7, and IL‐15 cytokines, and that this inability is responsible for the inhibition of PBMC adhesion‐related functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glucocorticoid‐induced down‐modulation of LFA‐ 1 and CD2 is reversible by cytokines that are produced in response to infection and/or inflammation.
glucocorticoid‐mediated inhibition of PBMC adhesion molecules can be reversed by cytokines that signal through the IL‐2 receptor γ‐chain.
glucocorticoid‐mediated inhibition of PBMC adhesion‐related functions can be reversed by cytokines that signal through the common γ chain.
